title: introduction-to-biology Mindmap
topicTitle: introduction to biology — interactive concept map
notes: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms, from molecules (DNA, proteins) to the entire biosphere. It encompasses branches such as Botany, Zoology,…
Biology: the study of living organisms (Greek: bios = life, logos = study).
Scope: from molecules (DNA, proteins) to cells, tissues, organs, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and the biosphere.

branches.topic: Introduction to Biology — Scope and Fields

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Biology: the study of living organisms.
Scope: from molecules to the biosphere (9 levels).
Branches: Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Genetics, Ecology, Physiology, Anatomy, Taxonomy, Biotechnology.
Characteristics of life: cellular, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response, evolution.
Scientific method: observation → hypothesis → experiment → conclusion.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Biology = Bios (life) + Logos (study) = the study of living organisms
Scope: molecule → cell → tissue → organ → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere
Scientific method: Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data → Conclusion

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms.
Life spans from molecules to the biosphere (9 organisational levels).
All living things share 7 fundamental characteristics.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Define biology and state its scope (9 levels).
List 8 branches of biology with one focus each.
State the 7 characteristics of life.
Biology = B-I-O (Basic, Investigative, Organic) = life study.
Characteristics: C-M-H-G-R-R-E (Cellular, Metabolism, Homeostasis, Growth, Reproduction, Response, Evolution).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Biology is NOT the same as medicine or agriculture; it is the foundational science, and medicine/agriculture…
Botany studies plants (including algae and fungi in some systems); Zoology studies animals.
Microbiology includes bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists; it overlaps with botany and zoology.

branches.topic: Relation of Biology with Other Sciences

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Biology is interconnected with Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and Earth Science.
Biochemistry: the chemistry of life (metabolism, enzymes, macromolecules).
Biophysics: physics applied to biology (nerve conduction, muscle, imaging).
Biostatistics: mathematics used in biology (genetics, populations, experiments).
Geobiology: interaction of life with Earth (fossils, climate, cycles).

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Biochemistry: metabolic pathways (glycolysis, Krebs, ETS) → energy (ATP)
Biophysics: nerve conduction (action potential), muscle mechanics, imaging (MRI)
Biostatistics: Punnett squares, Hardy-Weinberg, population models
Geobiology: fossil records, biogeochemical cycles, palaeoclimate

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Biology is an interdisciplinary science that relies on and contributes to other sciences.
Biochemistry studies the chemistry of living systems.
Biophysics applies physics to biological problems.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Explain how biology relates to chemistry (biochemistry).
Describe the role of physics in biology (biophysics).
Explain how mathematics is used in biology (biostatistics).
Biology = B-I-O (Bio-Interconnected with Other sciences).
Biochem = chemistry of life; Biophys = physics of life; Biostats = math of life.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Biochemistry is NOT the same as organic chemistry; it focuses on the chemistry of living systems…
Biophysics applies physics to biological problems; it is not "physics of life" in a vague sense.
Biostatistics is a branch of statistics, not a branch of biology; it is used BY biologists.
